name: Pairwise disjoint residue classes with distinct moduli in [20, 200] (largest reciprocal sum)
description: construct() -> classes [[m, r], ...] with distinct moduli 20 <= m <= 200 and 0 <= r < m, pairwise disjoint (r_1 != r_2 modulo gcd(m_1, m_2)). The score is the sum of 1/m (exact rational, reported as a float). Maximize. With moduli restricted to [20, 200] every valid construction bounds epsilon_19 from below.

sources.locator: Régis de la Bretèche, Kevin Ford and Joseph Vandehey, On non-intersecting arithmetic progressions (2013). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #1190 page inspected: epsilon_m, the largest sum 1/n_i over pairwise disjoint classes with moduli m < n_1 < ..., satisfies L(m)^(-1+o(1)) < epsilon_m < L(m)^(-sqrt(3)/2+o(1)) with L(m) = exp(sqrt(log m log log m)) (de la Bretèche, Ford and Vandehey), sharpened to epsilon_m = L(m)^(-1+o(1)) through the resolution of #202. No finite values are documented. With moduli restricted to [20, 200] every valid construction bounds epsilon_19 from below.
Erdős Problem #1190 (solved (Lean)); statement, history and current bounds reviewed 2026-09-24.
JSP-000995; pinned discovery source, independently paraphrased. Primary mathematical attribution follows the papers above.
